principles: Recovery must land the story in a phase where the flagged artifact is genuinely editable (INIT), not one that merely looks earlier.
Never weaken an existing safety invariant to add a convenience path; the INIT_CHECK scope-freeze stays intact.
Backward transitions are gated and auditable (reason required, pre-REVIEW only).
Fix the root cause of the path bug (main-root-relative worktree paths) rather than patching one call site.
drivers: A PLAN scope review can legitimately require a frozen title to change, and today there is no sanctioned way to do it for a worktree'd story.
The title/context freeze invariant (INIT_CHECK onward) must be preserved.
The round-trip must work entirely from inside the existing worktree with no git surgery.

options.name: Reopen to INIT via a gated PLAN->INIT transition (chosen)
pros: INIT is the only phase where checklist_update permits title/context edits, so this actually restores the capability.
Preserves the INIT_CHECK scope-freeze invariant untouched.
Natural re-advance path INIT->INIT_CHECK->PLAN re-runs the INIT review, so a changed title is re-validated.
cons: Requires a new machine edge + event + guard and the dev_start worktree-reuse fix so the re-advance reuses the worktree.
Slightly longer round-trip (re-run INIT review) than an in-place title edit.

options.name: Reopen to INIT_CHECK and remove INIT_CHECK from titleContextProtectedPhases (rejected)
pros: Matches the original (contradictory) guidance wording 'bounce to INIT_CHECK'.
cons: Weakens the scope-freeze invariant: making title editable at INIT_CHECK reopens the remove+re-add bypass the freeze was designed to prevent.
Still needs the dev_start path fix, so it is not actually simpler where it matters.

chosen: Reopen to INIT via a gated PLAN->INIT transition (chosen)
rationale: Reopening to INIT is the only option that actually restores the flagged-title recovery, because title/context is editable only at INIT; reopening to INIT_CHECK would require weakening the scope-freeze invariant (driver 2) for no real simplification, since the dev_start worktree-reuse path bug must be fixed either way. The chosen path adds a gated, auditable PLAN->INIT edge (reason required, PLAN-only) and fixes resolveWorktreePath to resolve the always-main-relative worktree path against the main repo root, so the re-advance INIT->INIT_CHECK reuses the existing worktree and re-runs the INIT review on the corrected title.

preMortem.scenario: The reopen becomes a way to weaken the INIT_CHECK scope-freeze invariant.
preMortem.trigger: A later change makes title/context editable at INIT_CHECK to shorten the round-trip.
preMortem.consequence: The remove+re-add scope bypass that the freeze was designed to prevent becomes possible again.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep INIT_CHECK in titleContextProtectedPhases; reopen targets INIT only; the round-trip smoke also asserts a title edit at INIT_CHECK stays rejected.

preMortem.scenario: The dev_start reuse fix breaks the from-main bootstrap path.
preMortem.trigger: resolveWorktreePath is changed to resolve story.worktree.path against the main repo root for all callers.
preMortem.consequence: A dev_start or worktree operation run from the main root resolves the wrong path.
preMortem.mitigation: story.worktree.path is always main-root-relative and getRepoRoot()==main when run from main, so from-main behavior is byte-identical; the round-trip smoke plus existing worktree smokes exercise both roots.

preMortem.scenario: PLAN->INIT reopen is abused to escape a legitimately failing PLAN->DEV gate.
preMortem.trigger: An agent reopens repeatedly to dodge scope review or a blocking gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Reopen requires a reason, is PLAN-only and owner-lease gated, and the return trip re-enters the full INIT->INIT_CHECK gate (scope-freeze + INIT review), so nothing downstream is bypassed.
